items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

ctx.x: Absolutely. And I can’t tell you why, but it goes back to the 30’s and 40’s I guess. And from my era, Vince Falcone, the pianist from Syracuse that became Frank Sinatra’s © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -19-

conductor, and Tony Bennett’s conductor; there was a guy named Torrie Zito of the Zito brothers, Torrie, Art and Ronnie. Ronnie is a drummer and when he was either 18 or 19 he was playing a gig with my former employer Jimmy Cavallo at the Beeches in Rome. Another story, this guy was in the main room with Bobby Darin, and it was the same situation, they heard this drummer and he became Bobby Darin’s drummer. Took him right out of Jimmy’s band. Artie Zito was a bass player. I don’t think he did much outside of…
And they mostly end with vowels.
